## Why is Razorpay a practical payment gateway choice for an Indian startup?


Razorpay is a practical first choice for an Indian startup that needs to start with one collection flow and evaluate additional payment products as it grows. Use[Payment Links](https://razorpay.com/payment-links/) for sales taken through messages,[Payment Pages](https://razorpay.com/payment-pages/) for a hosted collection page, or[Payment Gateway](https://razorpay.com/payment-gateway/) for a website or app checkout.


For a Shopify store, evaluate the[All-in-one Razorpay Payment Gateway app](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-gateway/ecommerce-plugins/shopify/) and its supported features. India is not on[Shopify Payments’ supported-country list](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/shopify-payments/supported-countries) as checked on 26 October 2026. Complete the required account and website review, and include the applicable Shopify and gateway charges in your launch budget.


## Why Is Choosing a Payment Gateway Harder for Indian Startups in 2026 Than It Used To Be?


India’s payments market has expanded and been re-regulated in the same 18 months. A provider that looked safe in 2024 may not meet the requirements set by the RBI’s September 2025 Master Direction today. Choosing a gateway now means evaluating regulatory standing alongside pricing and performance.


### How big is India’s digital payments market right now?


India’s digital payments market reached USD 10.43 billion in 2026, with a projected 22.27% CAGR through 2034. UPI alone processed 24.51 billion transactions in August 2026 worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore, up 22% year on year.


Digital payments now account for 99.7% of transaction volume in India. A gateway is no longer a growth lever. It is basic infrastructure, and it fails like infrastructure fails. For scale, 2,12,283 DPIIT-recognised startups as of 31 January 2026 are making some version of this decision.


### Why did the RBI tighten payment aggregator rules in September 2025?


The RBI issued a Master Direction on 15 September 2025 that consolidated three earlier frameworks into a single rulebook covering both bank and non-bank aggregators. It raised the bar on who can legally hold merchant settlement funds, tightened merchant KYC, and standardised escrow handling. Authorisation status is now a first-order selection criterion, not a footnote.


### Did You Know?


The RBI has not only approved payment aggregators. In February 2023, it returned 57 applications and told 17 operating aggregators to stop and wind down their online payment aggregation business. Picking an unauthorised provider is a business continuity risk, not just a compliance checkbox.


## What Does “Pricing” Actually Mean for a Payment Gateway, and Why Does the Headline Rate Mislead?


A payment gateway’s real cost is the MDR or platform fee, plus 18% GST on that fee, plus any setup or annual maintenance charge, divided by your actual payment success rate. Two gateways with identical headline rates can differ by lakhs a month once success rate and settlement delay are counted.


### The six-part true cost model every startup should use


1. **Direct transaction fee.** The MDR or platform fee per instrument. Card, UPI, netbanking, and EMI rarely price the same.
2. **GST on the fee.** 18% on the fee amount, not the transaction value. Frequently omitted from founder spreadsheets.
3. **Fixed costs.** Setup fee, annual maintenance charge, minimum monthly commitments.
4.


Include the gateway platform fee and applicable GST in your UPI cost model using the current contract and pricing page. Zero bank MDR does not make the gateway service free.


5. **Cost of failed transactions.** The biggest hidden line item. Revenue attempted minus revenue captured.
6. **Cost of delayed settlement.** Working capital locked in a slower settlement cycle.


An annual maintenance charge of Rs 10,000 at Rs 5,00,000 monthly volume adds roughly 0.16% to your effective rate, which quietly closes most “cheaper headline rate” gaps.


For bootstrapped startups doing under Rs 10 lakh monthly GMV, the fixed-cost bucket matters disproportionately. A Rs 10,000 AMC on Rs 3,00,000 monthly GMV adds 0.28% to your effective rate, more than many headline MDR differences. Several providers in India now offer zero setup fees and zero AMC on standard plans, making the entry cost genuinely zero beyond the per-transaction percentage. Razorpay’s standard plan carries no setup fee and no AMC.

Use[published pricing](https://razorpay.com/pricing/) to budget, the activation guidance above to plan launch, and your own completed-order data to assess performance. No universal success-rate claim establishes the result your startup will achieve.


## How should your startup budget for UPI payment acceptance?


Standard bank-to-bank UPI has zero bank MDR, while Razorpay charges a separate standard platform fee of 2% plus applicable GST unless your approved offer or contract specifies otherwise. Use the[current pricing page](https://razorpay.com/pricing/) and your contracted rates when budgeting.


## Comparing Payment Gateways on Pricing, Uptime and Support: The 8-Point Framework


Compare gateways on eight factors, not on the pricing page alone: onboarding speed, pricing transparency, payment method coverage, integration effort, uptime and reliability, compliance verification, support and escalation, and room to scale. Score each provider against these before a sales call, not after.


### The 8-point evaluation framework


1. **Onboarding speed.** Digital KYC that takes you live in days, not weeks of paperwork.
2. **Pricing transparency.** One clear rate per method, plus written disclosure of GST, AMC, and settlement cycle.
3. **Payment method coverage.** A missing method is a lost checkout, not a missing feature.
4. **Integration effort.** Real API documentation, SDKs, and a sandbox. Read the[developer documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/api) before the sales call.
5. **Uptime and reliability.** A stated figure, plus multi-bank smart routing.
6. **Compliance verification.** Current RBI authorisation and a dated PCI DSS assessment in writing.
7. **Support and escalation.** A named escalation path and a stated first-response time.
8. **Room to scale.** The same platform should work at 50x volume without a re-platform.

## What Does “Uptime” Really Mean for a Payment Gateway?


A published uptime percentage describes the gateway’s own infrastructure availability, not the UPI or bank rail it depends on. Real resilience comes from multi-bank smart routing and automatic failover, because even national rails have suffered documented multi-hour outages that no single uptime figure captures.


### What actually happened during India’s 2025 UPI outages


There were four separate UPI disruptions within roughly one month in 2025, with the 12 April incident lasting four to five hours. During the early-April disruption, transaction success rates fell to 50-60%. NPCI traced the April outage to excessive status-check requests from banks overwhelming capacity in the absence of a status check limiter.


A 99.9% gateway uptime figure would have been technically accurate throughout all of those events, and your checkout would still have been failing.


### How smart routing protects you from a single-rail failure


Routing and retry capabilities can help manage payment attempts, but their value depends on the available methods and the actual failures your checkout encounters. Assess completed orders and measured payment performance for your own method mix and period. Do not treat a universal success-rate or uptime percentage as a guarantee for your account.


### Did You Know?


At India’s transaction scale, even a UPI failure rate below 1% translates into millions of failed transactions daily. Percentage points are not abstract here. They are orders.
